title: Out-of-tree kube-scheduler plugins must be rebuilt for the 1.32 framework interfaces

detection.reason: whether a custom scheduler binary is in use is not visible in the inventory; the stock kube-scheduler image name is the only hint and a custom build can reuse it

quote: `PodEligibleToPreemptOthers` in the `preemption` interface now includes `ctx` in the parameters. Please update your plugins' implementation accordingly.
remediation: Only clusters running a custom-built kube-scheduler with out-of-tree plugins are affected. Rebuild the scheduler binary against the 1.32 framework (`PodEligibleToPreemptOthers` takes a ctx; `NodeToStatusMap` is a struct with accessor methods) before rolling the control plane.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l component=kube-scheduler -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.spec.containers[*].image}{"\n"}{end}'  # an image other than registry.k8s.io/kube-scheduler is a custom build that must be rebuilt for 1.32
coversNotes: Changed NodeToStatusMap from a map to a struct and exposed methods to access the entries.

title: In-place pod resize moves to the /resize subresource — clients that PATCH resources on the main Pod resource must change

detection.reason: which client resizes pods is a runtime behaviour, not a collected object

quote: A new /resize subresource was added to request pod resource resizing. Update your k8s client code to utilize the /resize subresource for Pod resizing operations.
remediation: Only relevant where InPlacePodVerticalScaling is enabled and a controller or script resizes running pods. Point it at `pods/<name>/resize`; RBAC for that client needs the `pods/resize` subresource.
verifyCommand: kubectl get clusterroles,roles -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.rules[]?.resources[]? == "pods/resize") | .kind + "/" + .metadata.name'  # empty means no principal can use the new subresource yet

title: DRA CEL selectors now have an enforced cost bound — expensive expressions are rejected at admission

detection.reason: ResourceClaim, ResourceClaimTemplate and DeviceClass are not collected; pods that reference claims are, so the hint names them

quote: The API server and scheduler now enforce an upper bound on the cost and runtime steps required for evaluating a CEL expression.
remediation: Review ResourceClaim / ResourceClaimTemplate / DeviceClass selectors that iterate over attribute strings; simplify any the API server rejects with a cost-limit error after the upgrade.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deviceclasses,resourceclaimtemplates -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | .kind + "/" + (.metadata.namespace // "-") + "/" + .metadata.name + ": " + ([.. | .expression? | strings] | join(" | "))'  # every CEL selector that will be cost-checked
coversNotes: DRA: CEL expressions using attribute strings exceeded the cost limit because their cost

title: fsGroup is now applied to ReadWriteOncePod volumes — ownership of existing files changes on next mount

detection.reason: the rule fires per PVC/pod pair; the projection carries PVC accessModes but not the fsGroup of the pod mounting it

quote: Apply fsGroup policy for ReadWriteOncePod volumes.
remediation: Pods with a `securityContext.fsGroup` mounting a ReadWriteOncePod PVC will have the volume's files re-owned on the first mount after the upgrade, as already happens for ReadWriteOnce. Check that applications relying on the previous (unchanged) ownership tolerate it, or set `fsGroupChangePolicy: OnRootMismatch` to limit the recursive chown.
verifyCommand: kubectl get pvc -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.accessModes | index("ReadWriteOncePod")) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name'  # each of these now gets fsGroup ownership applied

title: DRA opaque device configuration is capped at 10KiB at admission

detection.reason: DRA objects are not collected; pods that reference claims are, so the hint names them

quote: At admission time, Kubernetes enforces a 10KiB size limit.
remediation: ResourceClaims, ResourceClaimTemplates and DeviceClasses whose `opaque.parameters` exceed 10KiB are rejected after the upgrade; trim them before rolling the API server.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deviceclasses,resourceclaimtemplates,resourceclaims -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | .kind + "/" + (.metadata.namespace // "-") + "/" + .metadata.name + " " + ([.. | .opaque?.parameters? | select(. != null) | tojson | length] | add // 0 | tostring) + " bytes"'  # above 10240 is rejected at 1.32

title: DRA admin access now requires the DRAAdminAccess feature gate

detection.reason: DRA objects are not collected; pods that reference claims are, so the hint names them

quote: To allow admin access, starting with 1.32 the `DRAAdminAccess` feature gate must be enabled.
remediation: Any ResourceClaim / ResourceClaimTemplate that sets `adminAccess: true` stops being honoured unless `DRAAdminAccess=true` is set on kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler and kube-controller-manager.
verifyCommand: kubectl get resourceclaims,resourceclaimtemplates -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(any(..; .adminAccess? == true)) | .kind + "/" + .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name'  # these need DRAAdminAccess=true after 1.32

title: Structured authentication config rejects extra keys under k8s.io / kubernetes.io

detection.reason: the authentication configuration file lives in a component config file or flag on the control plane host, which is not a Kubernetes object the agent collects; the command reads it from the static pod's command line

quote: Disallow `k8s.io` and `kubernetes.io` namespaced extra key in structured authentication configuration.
remediation: If `--authentication-config` maps JWT claims to `extra` keys whose domain is `k8s.io` or `kubernetes.io` (or a subdomain), kube-apiserver refuses to start after the upgrade; rename the keys to your own domain.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l component=kube-apiserver -o json | jq -r '.items[].spec.containers[].command[]?, .items[].spec.containers[].args[]?' | grep -- --authentication-config  # then inspect that file's claimMappings.extra[].key on the control plane host

title: Soft eviction no longer overrides a pod's terminationGracePeriodSeconds

detection.reason: evictionMaxPodGracePeriod is kubelet configuration, not a collected object

quote: Fixed the bug where `spec.terminationGracePeriodSeconds` of the pod will always be overwritten by the MaxPodGracePeriodSeconds of the soft eviction, you can enable the `AllowOverwriteTerminationGracePeriodSeconds` feature gate, which will restore the previous behavior.
remediation: Where the kubelet's `evictionMaxPodGracePeriod` is set, soft-evicted pods now get min(pod grace period, evictionMaxPodGracePeriod) instead of always the eviction value; pods with a short own grace period terminate faster under pressure. Enable `AllowOverwriteTerminationGracePeriodSeconds` only if that is required.
verifyCommand: for n in $(kubectl get nodes -o name | cut -d/ -f2); do echo "== $n"; kubectl get --raw "/api/v1/nodes/$n/proxy/configz" | jq -c '.kubeletconfig | {evictionMaxPodGracePeriod, evictionSoft}'; done  # nodes with evictionSoft and a non-zero evictionMaxPodGracePeriod change behaviour

title: kube-scheduler no longer has the AzureDiskLimits / CinderLimits / EBSLimits / GCEPDLimits plugins

detection.reason: the scheduler configuration lives in a component config file or flag on the control plane host, which is not a Kubernetes object the agent collects; the command reads it from the static pod's command line

quote: Removed plugins AzureDiskLimits, CinderLimits, EBSLimits and GCEPDLimits if you explicitly enabled them in the scheduler config.
remediation: A KubeSchedulerConfiguration that names any of these plugins in `plugins.filter.enabled` / `plugins.preFilter.enabled` fails validation and the scheduler will not start. Remove them; the CSI limit is read from CSINode via the `NodeVolumeLimits` plugin.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l component=kube-scheduler -o json | jq -r '.items[].spec.containers[].command[]?, .items[].spec.containers[].args[]?' | grep -- --config  # then grep that file for AzureDiskLimits|CinderLimits|EBSLimits|GCEPDLimits

title: NodeRestriction now checks the audience of kubelet-requested service account tokens

detection.reason: the audiences a driver requests at runtime are not in the CSIDriver object; every CSIDriver is a candidate

quote: NodeRestriction admission now validates the audience value that kubelet is requesting a service account token for is part of the pod spec volume.
remediation: The kubelet may only request tokens whose audience appears in a pod's projected `serviceAccountToken` volume or in a CSIDriver's `tokenRequests`. A CSI driver whose deployed CSIDriver object omits `tokenRequests` for an audience it uses will fail to mount after the upgrade; the gate `ServiceAccountNodeAudienceRestriction` can be disabled as a temporary fallback. Source note: the gate is ON in 1.32.0 and 1.32.1, was reverted to OFF from 1.32.2 (the azureFile "failed to get service account token attributes" regression, #130015) and is ON again from 1.33 — a cluster upgrading to a 1.32.2+ patch does not meet it until 1.33.
verifyCommand: kubectl get csidrivers -o json | jq -r '.items[] | .metadata.name + ": " + ((.spec.tokenRequests // []) | map(.audience) | join(","))'  # a driver that uses tokens but lists no audience here will break
